title: Complete the interpreter mocks that produce optimizer feedback
motivation: The FIŘ interpreter runs the warmup and records the feedback that the optimizer speculates on. It failed on bounce, list_for, list_while, matrix_for and promise_reflect, because its mocks of R builtins lacked operations that these benchmarks use. So these benchmarks timed only the unspeculated baseline, with a regular `mkenv` and frame loads and stores of every variable. promise_reflect still fails after this range, because it also needs a `tryCatch` mock.
solution: `fir/interpret/internal/Builtins.java` extends the mocks. The generic `[[<-` and `[<-` grow a vector past its end, `[`, `[[`, `[<-` and `[[<-` accept name subscripts, and arithmetic, comparison, `abs` and `as.logical` keep or drop names like GNU-R. `matrix` and row-and-column subscripts work, with `InternalInterpreter#registerUnmatchedExternal` for a dynamic `x[[i, j]] <- v`. `environment()` and `ls` of a frame work. Also in this range: `[[` reads an absent list name as `NULL`, `[[` with `exact = FALSE` matches a unique name prefix, the name `""` never matches, and `ls` only accepts names that sort the same in the C and UTF-8 collations. A mock fails as unsupported where it does not copy GNU-R, for example for a logical matrix subscript or for `matrix` of empty data with a zero size.

files.repo-map.md: Adds entries for the nine new examples.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: Adds subscript growth, name subscripts, partial name matches for `exact = FALSE`, name propagation in arithmetic, `matrix`, matrix subscripts, `environment()` and `ls` to the interpreter mocks.
Adds `registerUnmatchedExternal`, which runs a mock for a dynamic call whose arguments do not match the function's parameters.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: Moves the module setup to `assertUnsupported`, and adds a test that a logical matrix subscript of `[` and `[<-` is unsupported.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: The warmup reads `x[i]` with `i` from 0.5 to 2.5, so it also reads a subscript below 1.
New example: `[`, `[[`, `[<-` and `[[<-` with the name `""`, which never matches, so reads are out of range and assignments append.
New example: `ls` of a frame that `sys.frame` returns.
New example: `matrix` of empty data with missing dimensions, which has one column.
New example: arithmetic, comparison, unary minus and `abs` of named vectors, to check which names the result keeps.
New example: `ls` of frames from `environment()`, with hidden names.
New example: `matrix` with missing or recycled arguments, and `[[`, `[`, `[[<-`, `[<-` with a row and column.
New example: `[[<-` and `[<-` past the end of lists and of integer, real and named string vectors.
New example: `[`, `[[`, `[<-` and `[[<-` with present, absent and appended name subscripts.
New example: `[[` with `exact = FALSE`, which matches a unique name prefix, and `[` with `drop`.
